liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **El Paso** (2 reviews): El Paso is entirely audience-recorded because the stage mics were not switched on; El Paso comes from an audience recording; reviewer wonders whether a soundboard exists [14][15]
- **Don't Ease Me In** (1 review): Reviewer says Don't Ease Me In moves along energetically [11]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Reviewer calls Eyes Of The World ripping [13]
- **China Doll** (1 review): Reviewer finds China Doll beautiful [17]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Reviewer recommends Bertha, along with Truckin' and Brokedown Palace, if listening only in part [15]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this The Other One among the best heard on the site [13]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Reviewer rates Wharf Rat highly for Jerry's clear enunciation of the lyrics and sustained notes [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-10-29.sbd.miller.32352.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 179 min; rated 4.56/5 by 16 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the mix as great; Sound by Charlie is very nice, but there are rough audience patches, mostly short except on El Paso; Reviewer praises the recording, singling out the bass and keyboards as fantastic [1][15][18][20]
- **gd73-10-29.sbd.powell-mollman.16817.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 181 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds Billy's mix poor with odd audio quirks, and the mix is adjusted during Wharf Rat [14]
- **gd1973-10-29.sbd.kaplan.1070.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 175 min; rated 4.23/5 by 13 [6]. Said about its sound: Noted flaws include a splice in Cold Rain And Snow, static in Eyes and Truckin', and a dropout in The Other One [6]
- **gd73-10-29.sbd.sacks.1014.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 174 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: Distortion appears on The Other One and Brokedown Palace when Jerry sings high notes [12]
- **gd1973-10-29.set2.131458.McIlhenny.flac16**: source not stated; 11 songs; 100 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [8]

## Around the show

- The date fell two years after Duane Allman died; a motorcycle stood onstage near the band, gone the next night [8]
- Reviewer finds the setlist itself unspectacular, though the performance and recording quality make the show worthwhile [11]
- Reviewer says this show holds its own against the Dane show, the following night, and the 1977 St. Louis show [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-10-29.sbd.miller.32352.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> DCassette (Tascam 122mkIII) -> Dat (Panasonic 3700/44.1k) D [1]. Also: Copied from Rob Eaton's DATs; patch source discs came from Matt Smith [1]
- **gd73-10-29.sbd.powell-mollman.16817.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSR > C > D > CD patched with AUD [3]
- **gd1973-10-29.sbd.kaplan.1070.shnf**: transferred by Thanks to Seth Kaplan for providing this show! Extraction and  SHN encoding of the source discs was done by S. Kaplan. Info file and notes by G.S. Hamilton; source: Reel master > 1 cassette gen > DAT > CD > SHN [6]
- **gd73-10-29.sbd.sacks.1014.sbefail.shnf**: source: MSR> C> DAT> Circulation> EAC> SHN [7]
- **gd1973-10-29.set2.131458.McIlhenny.flac16**: taped by Chaffe McIlhenny; transferred by Chaffe McIlhenny; source: Set 2, Handheld Sony 1 point stereo mic from the 5th and 4th row sometimes standing on chair; Recorderd and transferred by Chaffe McIlhenny; Master… [8]. Also: This set-two recording has several cuts between songs, including one in Big River, because the taper worried about running out of tape [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Kiel Auditorium - October 30, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/october-30-1973) [23]
